title: Explainable machine learning models enhance prediction of PFAS bioactivity using quantitative molecular surface analysis-derived representation.
authors: Yin, Zhipeng; Zhang, Min; Liu, Runzeng; Cai, Yong
one_liner_zh: 该文用QMSA描述符的机器学习模型预测PFAS与多个蛋白（含转录因子SMAD3/NRF2）的结合活性，并辅以分子对接和MD验证，虽涉及TF-DNA相关蛋白但非TF-DNA互作体系，方法可迁移但对象偏离核心。
abstract: The extensive use of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in industrial and consumer products poses health risks due to their toxicity. Computational toxicology approaches, particularly quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) models are essential for predicting PFAS bioactivity. However, established QSAR models including machine learning-based ones with traditional molecular descriptors such as constitutional, topological, and geometric descriptors, have limited predictive capability and interpretability. Herein, we proposed a novel machine learning approach that leverages quantitative molecular surface analysis (QMSA) of molecular electrostatic potential. Using QMSA descriptors, five machine learning models (e.g., random forest) achieved outstanding performance, with best accuracy of 0.950 +/- 0.017, AUC-ROC of 0.938 +/- 0.012, F1-score of 0.734 +/- 0.024, and MCC of 0.684 +/- 0.111 for five targets (tyrosyl-DNA phosphodiesterase 1 in the absence/presence of camptothecin, ATXN2 protein, transcription factor SMAD3, and transcription factor NRF2), which outperform previously reported models. SHAP analyses revealed that estimated density, molecular volume, positive surface area, and nonpolar surface area were the most important descriptors. These descriptors were deeply involved in PFAS binding to target proteins via non-covalent interactions as evidenced by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. Our results demonstrated that QMSA descriptors-based machine learning models are capable of predicting PFAS toxicity with extraordinary performance and interpretability. This study provides a novel machine learning framework for the high-throughput and cost-effective screening of high-risk emerging PFAS in aquatic environments. By identifying the contaminants that should be prioritized for regulation and treatment among the growing number of PFAS, our work aids in water quality monitoring and risk assessment, and guides decision-making in aquatic environmental management. Furthermore, this work enhances our understanding of the molecular mechanisms involved in PFAS bioactivity.
abstract_zh: 全氟和多氟烷基物质（PFAS）在工业和消费品中的广泛使用因其毒性而带来健康风险。计算毒理学方法，特别是定量结构-活性关系（QSAR）模型，对于预测PFAS生物活性至关重要。然而，已建立的QSAR模型，包括基于机器学习且使用传统分子描述符（如结构描述符、拓扑描述符和几何描述符）的模型，其预测能力和可解释性有限。在此，我们提出了一种新颖的机器学习方法，利用分子静电势的定量分子表面分析（QMSA）。使用QMSA描述符，五种机器学习模型（例如随机森林）实现了卓越的性能，针对五个靶标（酪氨酰-DNA磷酸二酯酶1在喜树碱存在/不存在情况下、ATXN2蛋白、转录因子SMAD3和转录因子NRF2）的最佳准确度为0.950 ± 0.017，AUC-ROC为0.938 ± 0.012，F1分数为0.734 ± 0.024，MCC为0.684 ± 0.111，优于先前报道的模型。SHAP分析揭示，估计密度、分子体积、正表面积和非极性表面积是最重要的描述符。这些描述符通过非共价相互作用深度参与PFAS与靶蛋白的结合，这一点通过分子对接和分子动力学模拟得到证实。我们的结果表明，基于QMSA描述符的机器学习模型能够以卓越的性能和可解释性预测PFAS毒性。本研究为水生环境中高风险新兴PFAS的高通量、成本效益筛选提供了一种新颖的机器学习框架。通过识别在日益增多的PFAS中应优先进行监管和处理的污染物，我们的工作有助于水质监测和风险评估，并指导水生环境管理中的决策。此外，这项工作增进了我们对PFAS生物活性所涉及分子机制的理解。
